protected_invariants: the canonical reader is not changed: readRequestLedger still refuses a ledger root without an entries/ directory and still does not create one, canonical reads still do not mutate restored state, and no canonical layout validation is relaxed to make a restore pass; the restore artifact is made correct before the reader sees it, because relaxing the reader would make every future generation's correctness unprovable

the repair is general rather than generation-specific: no generation id, timestamp, snapshot id, byte offset, machine path or provider is hard-coded anywhere in it, and the legacy derivation reads the versioned ledger contract rather than any fact about the one generation that happens to be on the target

the required-directory representation is enumerated from the same walk that produces the file list rather than inferred from it: a directory that holds no files leaves no trace in a file list, which is the defect, so 'required because the tree said so' is the only form of the claim that can be true

backward compatibility holds in both directions: a manifest that carries required_directories is authoritative, a manifest that does not is still admitted, verified and restored with its requirement re-derived from the canonical layout, and Object.hasOwn separates absent from present-and-empty so a generation that genuinely requires no directory is never guessed at

the restore writes the layout before the content, refuses any required directory that escapes the destination root, names a missing required directory as a missing required directory, and checks the directories before it asks the canonical readers anything -- so the descriptor-scoped ENOENT under /proc that a missing entries/ used to produce is not what an operator sees

staging cleanup is bounded to the one directory that exact invocation created: the name is minted locally with entropy drawn for it, never derived from anything the caller supplied; the destination is not a special case but simply a different path; a symbolic link inside the staging tree is unlinked and never entered; rmdir refuses a non-empty directory so something arriving late stops the cleanup rather than being deleted; and no preexisting destination or neighbour is ever named

a cleanup failure never hides the restore failure that caused it: the original error is the one reported, the cleanup note is appended best-effort, and an error that cannot carry a note is still the error that gets reported

the credential repair preserves every property the freeze existed for: credentials stay explicit and validated, no provider chain, no environment fallback, no profile fallback, no metadata service, no credential value in any log, report, error message or evidence file, session-token handling unchanged, describe() still reports a class and never a value, and no secret mutation is persisted back to disk; the freeze is kept on the transport's own record and only the object handed to the SDK is a private mutable copy

no runtime shim is required and none is used: no NODE_OPTIONS --require, no monkey patch, no temporary module injection, no manual mkdir of entries/, no post-restore repair, and the final validation runs with NODE_OPTIONS unset so RUNTIME_SHIM_REQUIRED=NO and MANUAL_EMPTY_DIRECTORY_REPAIR_REQUIRED=NO are measurements rather than claims
the reader, the offline CLIs, the live CLIs, the barrel, the verifier, the transports, the identity loader and the credential loader are byte-unchanged by this mission

no production state is mutated by this mission: no new generation is written, the existing remote generation is not overwritten or deleted, no object is written to or deleted from the off-host target, and the target is touched read-only for validation; no live fetch, DB write, raw write, training, prediction, backtest, model activation or migration apply is executed
Stage D is not started and no gate is advanced: BLOCKER_3 stays OPEN, GATE_2 stays NOT_ACCEPTED, GATE_3 stays NOT_AUTHORIZED and STAGE_D_STARTED=NO
forbidden_side_effects: writing, overwriting or deleting any object on the off-host target, and creating a second production generation
performing any DeleteObject or DeleteObjects anywhere, and adding a delete verb to the transport, the CLI surface or the documentation
changing src/infrastructure/market_evidence/authorityReader.js, stageDOperations.js or transactionStore.js, and relaxing canonical layout validation to make a restore pass
making a canonical read create a directory, and making restored state mutable to the readers
changing the offline CLIs, the live CLIs, the transport contract, the barrel or the verifier
adding a runtime dependency, and changing package.json or package-lock.json
requiring or introducing a runtime shim, a monkey patch, a temporary module injection, a manual mkdir or a post-restore repair
making any authenticated Cloudflare or provider API call, and creating, modifying or deleting any bucket
creating, requesting, rotating or inspecting any credential, and writing a credential value to argv, stdout, stderr, a log, an error message, a report or an evidence file
consuming Odds API quota, contacting B2, continuing a Cloudflare checkout, starting AWS provisioning, generating betting predictions or performing unrelated bookmaker work
formatting or repartitioning the off-host target machine, and weakening TLS anywhere
widening the backup credential to DeleteObject
merging any pull request, including this one, which stops at the merge gate
